name: Orbital station (LEO)
summary: ISS-class station in low Earth orbit. Sea-level cabin air, microgravity.

gravity_ms2.note: Continuous free fall in orbit: effective weight is near zero (microgravity).

p_kpa.note: Cabin held near sea-level pressure (14.7 psia).

temp_c.note: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6012 crew health limit (25 to 75% RH).

h_rate_msv_day.note: 80 to 160 mSv per six months, depending on the solar cycle. The engine uses the upper value.

neutrons.note: Secondary neutrons form wherever cosmic rays hit structure.

name: Lunar habitat (south polar)
summary: Pressurized surface habitat on NASA's exploration atmosphere: lower pressure, more oxygen.

p_kpa.note: 8.2 psia exploration atmosphere recommended by NASA. The Artemis surface habitat atmosphere is not final.

temp_c.note: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6012 crew health limit, applied as a design requirement.

h_rate_msv_day.note: Chang'E-4 surface measurement, unshielded. Used as an upper bound inside the habitat; shielding lowers it.

delay_s.note: Earth-Moon distance 363,300 to 405,500 km (S01) divided by the speed of light.

dust_class.note: Apollo crews carried dust into the cabin. Dust caused clogging, abrasion and seal problems; ground tests underestimated it.

neutrons.note: Neutral-particle dose about 3.1 µGy/h measured on the surface.

surface_temp_k.note: Equator, night to day. Context only: devices inside the habitat do not see it.

name: Lunar EVA (spacesuit)
summary: Moonwalk in a pressurized suit: pure oxygen at about 30 kPa, lunar gravity, abrasive dust.

p_kpa.note: Heritage EMU suit pressure (4.3 psi). Future lunar suits may differ.

temp_c.note: No published device-level suit-interior range found. Placeholder until verified.

delay_s.note: Earth-Moon distance (S01) divided by the speed of light.

m_carried_kg.note: Apollo A7LB suit, wet mass. Modern suits differ.

suit_self_support.unit: fraction of suit weight on the legs
suit_self_support.note: Pressurized suits partially (1 g) or completely (lunar g) carry their own weight. 0 = suit carries itself; 1 (conservative) = all suit weight goes through the legs.

transitions.label: Habitat cabin to suit (each EVA, device stays worn)

surface_temp_k.note: Equator, night to day. The suit's thermal control isolates worn devices from it.

name: Mars habitat
summary: Long-stay surface habitat. Mars gravity, minutes of light delay, months of transit.

p_kpa.note: Assumes the same exploration atmosphere as lunar habitats.

h_rate_msv_day.note: Curiosity RAD surface average, Aug 2012 to Jun 2013.

delay_s.note: Earth-Mars distance 54.6 to 401.4 million km (S02) divided by the speed of light: 3.0 to 22.3 min.

blackout.note: Solar conjunction disrupts links for about two weeks, roughly every two years.

dust_class.note: By analogy with Apollo cabin dust (S14). Martian soil contains perchlorate (S15).

surface_temp_k.note: Viking 1 site daily range; average about 214 K. Context only.

name: Mars EVA (spacesuit)
summary: Surface EVA on Mars. No Mars suit exists yet; suit values follow lunar heritage.

temp_c.note: No published device-level suit-interior range found. Placeholder until verified.

m_carried_kg.note: No Mars suit exists. Apollo A7LB wet mass assumed.

suit_self_support.unit: fraction of suit weight on the legs
suit_self_support.note: Full self-support is shown at lunar g (S23). At Mars g, partial support is likely; we keep the full 0 to 1 band.

transitions.label: Habitat cabin to suit (each EVA, device stays worn)
